Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions $\mathbf x_1$ and $\mathbf x_2,$ shown above. Find the fundamental matrix for the system.
examples.worked_solution:
Given a linear system $\mathbf{x}' = A \mathbf{x},$ where $A$ is an $n \times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $\Phi(t)$ of the system is an $n \times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our cases, we have a $2 \times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}=[\begin{aligned}4{e}^{5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 4\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}=[\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{5t} \\ 4{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14070844/assets/bb710709a593f8d185cde601fb5082d7f79ed21af824c28949477d2011479d95.png)

**Note:** The columns of $\Phi$ can be written in any order.
